findings.title: Hyphenated permissions bypass a ban
findings.description: `wholeActionShared` marks `deploy` as a compound fragment whenever it appears inside a compound on either side, even if it is the entire action in the prohibition. For `Never deploy` versus `Always deploy-staging`, the corroboration gate admits the pair, but the new clause check skips it; the permission can then be stored despite the ban.

evidence.explanation: `maskedCompoundParts` supplies `deploy` from the permission to the union at lines 1198–1203, making `wholeActionShared` false. Both rules qualify as short at the corroboration gate, while the clause gate's single-shared-word branch now requires that false value; `addMemoryEntry` relies on detected conflicts to reject the write.

findings.title: Quoted examples let opposing rules coexist
findings.description: `collapsedActionSize` now masks quoted compounds before collapsing them, but the corroboration caller still supplies unmasked `contentWords`, leaving the quoted parts in its size. For `Never merge 'auto-merge'` versus `Always merge`, the extra `auto` makes the first rule too long for `shortPair`; without vector confirmation, the pair is discarded before its direct polarity flip is checked.

evidence.explanation: `contentWords` includes quoted words, whereas the new `maskedCompoundParts` omits them. The `shortPair` caller combines those two representations, and the corroboration condition skips `polarityClash` when its size check fails and no other admission condition applies.

findings.title: Unrelated rules are rejected as conflicts
findings.description: `collapsedActionSize` treats each hyphenated action as one word, but the clause gate still counts a shared fragment such as `auto` as the entire shared action. With an existing `Never auto-merge` entry, adding `Always auto-deploy` now passes both the shortened-pair admission and clause-clash checks, so `addMemoryEntry` rejects an unrelated rule as a contradiction; a pinned entry makes that rejection final.
findings.code_snippet: +      const shorter = Math.min(collapsedActionSize(negMasked, neg), collapsedActionSize(permMasked, perm));

evidence.explanation: Both texts contain three content words but collapse to two, admitting their sole shared word `auto` through the new short-pair check. Their different compounds receive no pairwise discount, while each masked action collapses from two words to one; the new `shorter` value therefore satisfies the whole-action clash test. The distinct-target exclusion does not apply because neither `merge` nor `deploy` is a trailing object of the shared word `auto`, and the conflict path rejects the write.

findings.title: Opposite hyphenated actions coexist
findings.description: `polarizedClausesClash` discounts the two parts of an identical hyphenated action but compares the reduced overlap against the original two-word clause size. For `Never auto-deploy` and `Always auto-deploy`, the corroboration gate admits the pair, but the clause gate finds no clash, so the opposing rule bypasses conflict rejection.
findings.code_snippet:
+      const discount = compoundSharedDiscount(neg, perm, negMasked, permMasked);
+      const shared = Math.max(0, rawShared - discount);

evidence.explanation: `contentWords` splits `auto-deploy` into two words; the new helper discounts their identical compound by one. The short-pair corroboration admits the rules, but the clause gate requires either two shared words or a shared count equal to the unchanged shorter size of two. A missed conflict proceeds past the rejection path.

findings.title: Quoted examples hide direct conflicts
findings.description: `polarizedClausesClash` supplies raw clauses to `compoundSharedDiscount` even though it counts action words from quote-masked clauses. For `Never force push (the command 'force-push')` versus `Always force-push`, the quoted example creates a compound match that discounts the genuine, unquoted action overlap, allowing the opposing rules past conflict rejection.
findings.code_snippet:
+      const discount = compoundSharedDiscount(neg, perm, negMasked, permMasked);
+      const shared = Math.max(0, rawShared - discount);

evidence.explanation: `maskedActionWords` excludes the quoted `force-push`, leaving the prohibition's unquoted `force` and `push` as action words. The new helper instead scans the raw clauses, finds `force-push` on both sides, and subtracts one from that two-word overlap; the same raw-text discount also reduces corroboration.

findings.title: Real conflicts disappear with overlapping names
findings.description: `compoundSharedDiscount` subtracts `parts.length - 1` for each matching compound even though `sharedCount` counts each stemmed part only once. When opposite-action entries contain overlapping compounds such as `pi-config` and `pi-config-sidecar`, the discount can push their shared count below both conflict gates’ thresholds before contradiction detection.
findings.code_snippet:
+    if (parts.length >= 2 && parts.every((p) => aWords.has(p) && bWords.has(p))) {
+      discount += parts.length - 1;

evidence.explanation: `sharedCount` counts distinct shared words, while lines 1894-1895 deduct a contribution independently for each matching compound. For `Never publish pi-config-sidecar and pi-config` versus `Always publish pi-config-sidecar and pi-config`, the shared words are `publish`, `pi`, `configuration`, and `sidecar`; the helper deducts three and leaves one, below the two-word thresholds at the corroboration gate (line 1863) and clause gate (lines 1164-1165).

findings.title: New conflict logic has no diagnostics
findings.description: The modified conflict-gate logic and new `compoundSharedDiscount` helper add executable branches without any `log.debug`, `log.info`, `log.warn`, or `log.error` call in the changed code region. When the new discount changes a candidate decision, operators receive no logger-backed context explaining the compound match or adjusted shared count.

evidence.explanation: The checklist requires every modified runtime code region to contain a logging call wired through `createLogger`. The changed shared-word calculation and newly added helper contain no logging call, although the file has a logger available.

citations.citation: Log all new or modified runtime code using createLogger (tests excluded)

findings.title: Some brand conflicts are falsely retained
findings.description: `compoundSharedDiscount` stems compound parts before checking `STOP_WORDS`, whereas `contentWords` removes stop words before stemming. A hyphenated compound containing a raw stop word therefore fails the all-parts check, receives no discount, and can retain the false shared-word overlap that this change is intended to remove.

evidence.explanation: The changed helper maps each raw compound part through `stem` before checking `STOP_WORDS`, while the existing content-word implementation filters the raw token first. This makes the helper's required-part set inconsistent with the sets passed into it and can leave the original false overlap counted.
